at-0001.title: Round money only with round_money
at-0001.content: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

at-0003.title: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes
at-0003.content: Signal domain failures by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with stable snake_case codes such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` and `negative_amount`; reuse `invalid_state` with the message `f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}"` for non-draft invoices.

at-0007.title: Money-moving functions take idempotency_key
at-0007.content: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. refund in ledgerly/adjustments.py) must accept keyword-only idempotency_key=None, check ledgerly.audit.events() for an existing entry with that key first and return the original record without reapplying, and include idempotency_key in the audit entry.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
